/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 16 April 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2523 (39)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4026 (62)
Baltic Panamax Index: 1970 (22)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1398 (27)
Baltic Handysize Index: 730 (15)
CAPESIZE
The market took a breather today following a strong run earlier in the week, with the BCI 182 5TC edging up a more modest $562 to settle at $36,515. Despite the index posting another gain, underlying performance softer, suggesting a degree of consolidation at current levels. C5 slipped marginally by $0.250 to $13.280, while C3 remained largely flat, easing slightly by $0.064 to $32.377. In the Pacific, sentiment cooled, with the market correcting after recent gains. Two miners were active on C5, though this did little to prevent rates from easing, with offers starting around $14.00 before fixtures were concluded closer to $13.25. In the Atlantic, sentiment remains upbeat, though activity was more subdued following several hectic days. The market is pausing for breath, but underlying fundamentals continue to provide support. This was reflected in C8, where stronger transatlantic fixtures overnight pushed rates up by $3,787 to $36,756. The ballaster list for May arrivals in South Brazil and West Africa has tightened significantly, while supply in the North Atlantic also remains constrained.
PANAMAX
Another firmer day across both basins with sentiment still optimistic. The P1A increased today by $379 to mark at $14,270 which is more of a reflection of the stronger transatlantic grains market which appears to be paying a premium over mineral trades. Fronthaul grains are said to be pushing with reported fixtures reflecting this increase in cargo supply with owners reportedly resisting revising downwards and instead bids are improving to secure tonnage. In Asia the same improved market tone continues as the P3A and P5 reflected firmer gains with offers being hit. This is especially apparent for the longer trades from Indonesia and Australia. Period activity remains evident with the scrubber fitted XH Square Leg (83,070 2024) open in Qingdao 20/21 April was said to have fixed by some for 11/13 months redelivery worldwide at close to $21,000 with the scrubber benefit for charterers account to Aquavita while others are saying she fixed for laden legs. The P5TC climbed $202 to conclude at $17,730.

Atlantic
Refined Success fixed the JY Shanghai (81,090 2020) open in Gibraltar 21/24 April for a NC South America trip to Singapore-Japan range with grains at $28,000, although some have reported the rate to be $27,500. Jera GM covered on subjects their Baltimore to Amsterdam 75,000/10% stem for 1/10 May but further details were lacking.

Asia
The scrubber fitted London I (82,052 2025) open Dhamra 20 April fixed a trip via EC India to WC India with coal at $23,000, further details remain to be seen.

SUPRAMAX
Like the smaller Handysize, the only rather subdued area remained the Continent-Mediterranean as persistent limited fresh enquiry remained, otherwise most areas gained traction. The US Gulf saw increased activity and rates remained firm brokers said especially for the trans Atlantic runs, although demand was also in play for fronthaul. Positive movement from the South Atlantic certainly again for Atlantic orientated business. From the Indian Ocean again some health numbers were being discussed with increased coal demand from India and Pakistan. Further East, again brokers said that stronger levels were being discussed with demand remaining both for backhaul business and from the NoPac. Period activity was seen with talk of the Mandarin China (56,778 2011) open Makassar 22 April being fixed for short period at $17,500 but no more details surfaced. The 11TC average closed up a further $339 at $17,699.

Atlantic
The Letizia (61,288 2015) open Piombino 11/13 April was heard fixed basis delivery Garrucha for a trip redelivery EC United States at $10,750 with clinker by Drylog. The Medi Vaiano (60,386 2016) open Sept-Îles was heard fixed basis delivery Norfolk for a trip redelivery Egypt at $22,500 with grains to Refined Success. Also, the Africa Hope (53,416 2009) open Calabar 19 April was linked to fixing a cargo of nickel ore at $37.00 pmt from San Pedro to Lanshan basis 25,000 shinc load and 12000 shinc discharge nut again further details remained lacking.

Asia
The Cumbria (61,628 2015) open Mombasa 15/22 April was heard to have fixed via South Africa discharge EC India and redelivery Singapore at $20,000 to Norden. the Gemini Honor (56,830 2011) Fujairah 28/30 April was placed on subjects at $19,500 for Arabian Gulf fronthaul to SE Asia but others said it was to EC India. The Azul (63,253 2014) open Port Luis 15/18 April fixed via Port Elizabeth and EC India redelivery Singapore at $19,000 with Jeyst but some heard it was closer to $19,500. The African Finfoot (61,219 2016) Dar es Salaam 20 Apr heard fixed at $23,500 plus $235,000 ballast bonus basis delivery Richards Bay for a trip Pakistan however some heard this had failed.

HANDYSIZE
A positive day overall for the sector, although the Atlantic remained somewhat positional. Sentiment remained relatively subdued from the Continent-Mediterranean with brokers saying that little fresh enquiry was entering into the market. That said, positive moment was seen from both the North and South Atlantic as better levels of fresh enquiry were seen which gave then owning side a bit more encouragement. Continuing from yesterday the Asian also made gains as demand increased and period interest gained traction. The Vinaship Harmony (28,201 2010) open Tabaco 24/26 April was heard to have been fixed for short period in high $8,000s to Well Reach. The 7 TC average gained $268 to finish at $13,143.

Atlantic
The Lignum Link (42,564 2024) was heard fixed for an inter Caribbean business, although some said she might have fixed in-house, but no more details surfaced. The African Nightjar (39,758 2015) open Leixoes 16 April was rumoured to have fixed from the Continent to EC Mexico with Pangaea but again no more details surfaced.

Asia
The Pochard (37,991 2023) open Onsan 21/22 April was heard fixed for 2/3 laden legs at $16,500 with Ultrabulk, but further details were not disclosed. The Sinlau Bulker (34,485 2018) open Singapore was placed on subjects in the $16,000s for multiple legs by Swire, again further details remained under wraps. The Norse Innoshima (40,058 2024) open Hakata 19 April fixed around $17,000 also for multiple legs, the first leg understood to be clinker into Australia. Otherwise, the Sakura Dream (38,213 2013) was heard fixed basis delivery CJK for a trip Malaysia with intention rock phosphate at $13,500 for the first 25 day then a split rate with Cosfar. A 33,000 open Japan 16 April was also heard fixed at around $12,000 for a trip with generals via Bohai Bay to Malaysia also with Cosfar.

Market Fundamentals

Trading Commentary
Cape
The Cape FFA market was volatile today, particularly the May contract, trading between a range of 32750-33750. As expected, Apr was stable with a range of 30150-30250. The May v Jun roll widened and strengthened up to +400, with the June trading between 32750 and 33500. Q2 was thin with a few clips going through up to 32150. Activity on the Q3 was good with a wide range of 30250-30900, while the Q4 struggled for similar liquidity, with a range of 30200-30650. The Q3 v Q4 spread was marginally firmer trading +200. Cal27 was volatile also with prints early on up to 25800, then back down to 25400. Cal28 traded a few times at 22900.

PMX
PMX papers came under slight pressure today, easing across the curve following yesterday’s push higher, and despite the positive index of +202 it seemed relatively offered. Apr traded from 17400 down to 17250, while May traded down to lows of 18950 and was bid up to 19100. Jun also drifted down, valued at a 19300 at close, leaving Q2 around 18550. Q3 started at 18600, traded down to 18400 and closed around 18500, while Q4 traded between 17100 and 16800. Cal 27 moved from 14850 to 14650. Overall, the market saw a modest pullback across the curve.

SMX + HANDY
The SMX curve came under some pressure first thing and the curve stepped down from previous days close where it found a level, and traded the rest of the day between a narrow range in fits and starts. Apr started the day trading 15100 but found some traction trading back up to 15350, while May changed hands between 16900 and 16700 and Jun traded to a low of 16750. Q2 traded at 16100, while Q3 traded from 16400 to a low of 16000 and Q4 15100 – 15000. Cal37 traded a few times 12925 – 12800 and the Cal28 at 12000. Handy was a touch softer, with May trading 15200, May+Jun trading 15000, Q2 trading 14500 and Q3 at 14500.

Carbon
EU carbon markets pushed 1.1% higher today, despite below-average traded volumes. Today's EU Common compliance auction settled 2.7m EUAs at €72.40/eua, below last night's daily spot futures close and dragging the market lower during morning trade. However, the futures market rebounded at midday with the benchmark Dec26 contract reaching an intraday high of €75.80/eua before settling at €74.96/eua, up €0.80/eua, during the assessment window.

a few clips going through up to 32150. Activity on the Q3 was
good with a wide range of 30250-30900, while the Q4
struggled for similar liquidity, with a range of 30200-30650.
The Q3 v Q4 spread was marginally ﬁrmer trading +200.
Cal27 was volatile also with prints early on up to 25800, then
back down to 25400. Cal28 traded a few times at 22900.
PMX
PMX papers came under slight pressure today, easing across
the curve following yesterday’s push higher, and despite the
positive index of +202 it seemed relatively oﬀered. Apr
traded from 17400 down to 17250, while May traded down to
lows of 18950 and was bid up to 19100. Jun also drifted
down, valued at a 19300 at close, leaving Q2 around 18550.
Q3 started at 18600, traded down to 18400 and closed
around 18500, while Q4 traded between 17100 and 16800.
Cal 27 moved from 14850 to 14650. Overall, the market saw
a modest pullback across the curve.
SMX + HANDY
The SMX curve came under some pressure ﬁrst thing and the
curve stepped down from previous days close where it found
a level, and traded the rest of the day between a narrow
range in ﬁts and starts. Apr started the day trading 15100
but found some traction trading back up to 15350, while May
changed hands between 16900 and 16700 and Jun traded to
a low of 16750. Q2 traded at 16100, while Q3 traded from
16400 to a low of 16000 and Q4 15100 – 15000. Cal37 traded
a few times 12925 – 12800 and the Cal28 at 12000. Handy
was a touch softer, with May trading 15200, May+Jun trading
15000, Q2 trading 14500 and Q3 at 14500.Cape 180 5TC

As expected, Apr was stable with a range of 30150-30250. The May v Jun roll widened and strengthened up to +400, with the June trading between 32750 and 33500. Q2 was thin with a few clips going through up to 32150. Activity on the Q3 was good with a wide range of 30250-30900, while the Q4 struggled for similar liquidity, with a range of 30200-30650. The Q3 v Q4 spread was marginally firmer trading +200. Cal27 was volatile also with prints early on up to 25800, then back down to 25400. Cal28 traded a few times at 22900. PMX PMX papers came under slight pressure today, easing across the curve following yesterday’s push higher, and despite the positive index of +202 it seemed relatively offered. Apr traded from 17400 down to 17250, while May traded down to lows of 18950 and was bid up to 19100. Jun also drifted down, valued at a 19300 at close, leaving Q2 around 18550. Q3 started at 18600, traded down to 18400 and closed around 18500, while Q4 traded between 17100 and 16800. Cal 27 moved from 14850 to 14650. Overall, the market saw a modest pullback across the curve. SMX + HANDY The SMX curve came under some pressure first thing and the curve stepped down from previous days close where it found a level, and traded the rest of the day between a narrow range in fits and starts. Apr started the day trading 15100 but found some traction trading back up to 15350, while May changed hands between 16900 and 16700 and Jun traded to a low of 16750. Q2 traded at 16100, while Q3 traded from 16400 to a low of 16000 and Q4 15100 – 15000. Cal37 traded a few times 12925 – 12800 and the Cal28 at 12000.
